# FDG8058

> CONSIDER overloading comparison operators (<, >,<=, >=) whenever you implement `IComparable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.6 IComparable&lt;T> and IEquatable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1036
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test suggestion
- Status: verified

CA1036 reports an externally visible type that implements IComparable or IComparable<T> without the operators ==, !=, <, <=, > and >= and an Equals override (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so it also asks for the equality members of FDG8056 and FDG8100. Section 5.7 (FDG5081 to FDG5087) decides when operators are worth overloading. The SDK code fix adds the operators but also Equals and GetHashCode overrides that throw NotImplementedException (probe), so autofix is no.

## From the book

```csharp
public struct Decimal : IComparable< Decimal >, ... {
   public int CompareTo(Decimal other){ ... }
   public static bool operator<(Decimal x, Decimal y) {
     return x.CompareTo(y)<0;
   }
   public static bool operator>(Decimal x, Decimal y) {
     return x.CompareTo(y)>0;
   }
   ...
}
```

See section 5.7 for details on when to overload operators.
